verdict: Ads paused four days; leads dropped sharply — resumption gated on efficiency.
narrative: Both Meta and Google ran dark from September 17–20, producing zero leads across those four days and driving a 58% drop in leads week-over-week. Before the pause, cost per lead had already climbed to roughly $21 — above the 28-day average of $16.66 — so campaigns are being reviewed for efficiency before spend resumes rather than simply switching back on. On the tracking side, Google's conversion measurement appears broken, meaning $444 in Google spend this period has no recorded return; a fix is in progress. Once attribution is clean and the efficiency gate is cleared, you should see a more stable lead flow heading into October.
